about.title: About NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
about.blurb: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 provides guidance to industry, government agencies, and other organisations to manage cybersecurity risks. It offers a taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes that can be used by any organisation — regardless of its size, sector, or maturity — to better understand, assess, prioritise, and communicate its cybersecurity efforts.

p: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, published in February 2024, is a voluntary framework that provides organisations with a common language and systematic methodology for managing cybersecurity risk. It was developed through a collaborative process involving industry, government, and academia.

CSF 2.0 introduces a new sixth function — GOVERN — which sits at the centre of the framework and underscores that cybersecurity risk management must be embedded in organisational strategy, not treated as a purely technical concern.

The framework is designed to complement, not replace, existing cybersecurity programmes and risk management processes. It can be applied alongside other standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-53, and CIS Controls.

l: GOVERN (GV) — Establishes the organisational context, strategy, roles, and oversight needed to manage cybersecurity risk. New in CSF 2.0.
IDENTIFY (ID) — Helps the organisation understand its assets, risks, and improvement priorities.
PROTECT (PR) — Supports the ability to safeguard assets and limit the impact of cybersecurity events.
DETECT (DE) — Enables timely discovery of cybersecurity events and anomalies.
RESPOND (RS) — Supports the ability to contain and manage the impacts of a detected cybersecurity incident.
RECOVER (RC) — Supports timely restoration of normal operations and capabilities impaired by a cybersecurity incident.

p: The CSF Core is organised as a hierarchy: Functions → Categories → Subcategories. There are 6 Functions, 22 Categories, and 106 Subcategories. Each Subcategory represents a specific cybersecurity outcome — a concise statement of what 'good' looks like.

Organisations use the framework by creating Profiles — mappings of the CSF outcomes to their business requirements, risk tolerance, and resources. A 'Current Profile' captures the present state; a 'Target Profile' captures desired outcomes. The gap between them guides prioritisation.

CSF 2.0 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 are complementary. ISO 27001 specifies requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and is certifiable; CSF 2.0 provides outcome-focused guidance and a risk communication vocabulary.

Mapping between the two frameworks allows organisations to demonstrate alignment with both without duplicating effort. Many ISO 27001 Annex A controls map directly to CSF 2.0 subcategories, enabling joint gap analyses and integrated audit programmes.

groups.name: GOVERN
groups.desc: The organisation's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored. GOVERN is new in CSF 2.0 and provides the overarching context for all other functions.

sections.name: Organizational Context
sections.desc: The circumstances surrounding the organisation's cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood

items.name: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
items.desc: The organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management.
achieved: The organisational mission, vision, and strategic objectives are documented and reviewed regularly.
Cybersecurity risk tolerance is explicitly tied to and informed by the organisational mission.
Senior leadership has approved and communicates the connection between mission and cybersecurity priorities.
Business impact analyses reference the mission when classifying critical services and assets.
evidence: Organisational mission statement linked to cybersecurity risk appetite documentation
Board-approved cybersecurity strategy aligned to mission objectives
Risk tolerance statement referencing mission-critical functions
Business impact analysis referencing mission-critical processes

items.name: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood
items.desc: Internal and external stakeholders are determined, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood.
achieved: An interested-parties register identifies all internal and external stakeholders relevant to the ISMS.
Stakeholder cybersecurity requirements (regulatory, contractual, operational) are documented and reviewed.
Communication channels exist to receive and respond to stakeholder cybersecurity concerns.
Stakeholder requirements are reflected in the organisation's cybersecurity objectives and policies.
evidence: Interested-parties register with documented requirements per stakeholder group
Regulatory and contractual obligations log reviewed at least annually
Minutes of stakeholder engagement meetings referencing cybersecurity topics
Cybersecurity objectives traceable to stakeholder requirements

items.name: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed
items.desc: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity — including privacy and civil liberties obligations — are understood and managed.
achieved: A compliance register catalogues all applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations affecting cybersecurity.
Controls are mapped to legal and regulatory requirements, with ownership assigned.
Changes in legal or regulatory requirements are tracked and trigger reviews of affected controls.
Privacy obligations are integrated into cybersecurity risk management processes.
evidence: Legal and regulatory compliance register (e.g., GDPR, NIS2, sector-specific regulations)
Contractual obligation tracker with assigned owners
Evidence of monitoring regulatory change (e.g., legal update subscriptions, regulator communications)
Data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) or privacy risk assessments

items.name: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
items.desc: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organisation are understood and communicated.
achieved: Critical services and capabilities are identified from the perspective of external stakeholders.
Service level commitments are documented and linked to cybersecurity resilience requirements.
Stakeholder dependencies are incorporated into business continuity and incident response planning.
Communication processes exist to notify affected stakeholders of significant service disruptions.
evidence: Service catalogue or critical service register with external stakeholder dependencies noted
SLA or contractual commitments referencing cybersecurity availability targets
Business continuity plan referencing external stakeholder dependencies
Stakeholder communication plan for incident and outage notifications

items.name: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
items.desc: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organisation depends on are understood and communicated.
achieved: Dependencies on third-party services, utilities, and technology are identified and documented.
Critical dependencies are incorporated into risk assessments and continuity plans.
Single points of failure arising from dependencies are identified and treated.
Dependency information is kept current and reviewed at defined intervals.
evidence: Third-party and supply chain dependency register
Business impact analysis identifying critical external dependencies
Risk treatment records for high-priority dependency risks
Evidence of periodic review and update of dependency register

items.name: Conformance requirements are understood and met
items.desc: Conformance requirements — whether from law, regulation, contract, or internal policy — are understood and met.
achieved: The organisation maintains a current list of applicable conformance requirements (standards, frameworks, certifications).
Conformance gaps are identified through formal assessments and tracked to closure.
Certification and audit activities are planned to demonstrate ongoing conformance.
Non-conformities are recorded, analysed for root cause, and resolved in a timely manner.
evidence: Conformance requirements register (e.g., ISO 27001, PCI DSS, Cyber Essentials)
Gap assessment reports with remediation tracking
Certification or audit schedule and reports
Non-conformity log with corrective action records

sections.name: Risk Management Strategy
sections.desc: The organisation's priorities, constraints, risk tolerance, and assumptions are established and used to support operational risk decisions

items.name: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
items.desc: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.
achieved: Cybersecurity risk management objectives are formally defined and aligned with business objectives.
Objectives are approved by senior leadership and communicated across the organisation.
Objectives are reviewed at defined intervals and updated when the business context changes.
Progress against risk management objectives is tracked and reported to leadership.
evidence: Risk management strategy or framework document signed off by senior leadership
Cybersecurity risk management objectives documented in ISMS documentation
Meeting minutes showing leadership approval of risk objectives
Periodic reports on progress against risk management objectives

items.name: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
items.desc: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained.
achieved: A formal risk appetite statement is approved by senior leadership and the board.
Risk tolerance thresholds are defined and used to guide risk treatment decisions.
The risk appetite is communicated to all relevant staff and stakeholders.
Risk appetite and tolerance statements are reviewed at least annually or when the business context changes significantly.
evidence: Board or executive-approved risk appetite statement
Risk tolerance thresholds documented in the risk management framework
Evidence of communication to relevant stakeholders (e.g., all-hands briefings, policy acknowledgements)
Records of periodic review and approval of risk appetite statement

items.name: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
items.desc: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes.
achieved: Cybersecurity risks appear in the enterprise risk register alongside other business risks.
Cybersecurity risk reporting follows the same cadence and format as enterprise risk reporting.
Risk owners for cybersecurity risks are aligned with enterprise risk ownership structures.
Cybersecurity risk aggregation and escalation thresholds are integrated with enterprise risk governance.
evidence: Enterprise risk register with cybersecurity risks included
Risk committee or board meeting minutes discussing cybersecurity risks
Integrated risk reporting dashboard or report
Evidence of cybersecurity risk escalation through enterprise risk governance

items.name: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
items.desc: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated.
achieved: The organisation's risk treatment preferences (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) are documented and communicated.
Risk response criteria guide consistent decision-making across risk owners.
Risk treatment options are evaluated for cost-effectiveness relative to risk reduction.
Residual risk acceptance criteria are defined and approved by appropriate authorities.
evidence: Risk management framework or policy defining risk response options
Risk treatment criteria communicated to risk owners
Risk treatment plans with cost-benefit analysis
Residual risk acceptance records signed by appropriate authority

items.name: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
items.desc: Lines of communication across the organisation are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties.
achieved: Escalation paths for cybersecurity risks are defined and communicated.
Third-party and supply chain cybersecurity risks are reported through the same governance structures as internal risks.
Risk communication is two-way: leadership communicates priorities, practitioners communicate emerging risks.
Risk reporting formats and cadences are standardised to facilitate aggregation and comparison.
evidence: Risk escalation and communication procedures
Risk reporting templates with defined audience and frequency
Evidence of third-party risk communication (e.g., vendor risk reports reviewed at risk committee)
Documented escalation path for critical cybersecurity risks

items.name: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
items.desc: A standardised method for calculating, documenting, categorising, and prioritising cybersecurity risks is established and communicated.
achieved: A risk assessment methodology is documented and applied consistently across the organisation.
Risk scoring criteria (likelihood and impact) are defined with calibrated scales.
Risk categorisation schema allows aggregation of similar risk types.
Risk prioritisation outputs are used to inform investment and treatment decisions.
evidence: Risk assessment methodology documentation
Risk scoring matrix with likelihood and impact definitions
Risk register with consistent categorisation applied
Evidence that risk prioritisation drives resource allocation decisions

items.name: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
items.desc: Strategic opportunities (positive risks) are characterised and included in organisational cybersecurity risk discussions.
achieved: The organisation's risk process considers both threats and opportunities arising from cybersecurity investments.
Positive risk opportunities (e.g., competitive advantage from strong security posture) are documented.
Opportunity assessments are presented alongside threat risk assessments in governance forums.
Cybersecurity investments are evaluated for their potential to enable business opportunities.
evidence: Risk register or assessment process that includes opportunity identification
Business case documentation linking cybersecurity investment to business opportunity
Board or risk committee discussions on cybersecurity-enabled opportunities
Strategic planning documents referencing cybersecurity as a business enabler

sections.name: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
sections.desc: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement are established and communicated

items.name: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
items.desc: Organisational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture of cybersecurity risk awareness.
achieved: The board and executive leadership formally accept accountability for cybersecurity risk management.
Leadership visibly champions cybersecurity initiatives and communicates their importance to all staff.
Cybersecurity metrics and risk posture are regularly reported to and discussed by leadership.
A culture of security awareness is promoted through leadership behaviour and resource allocation.
evidence: Board or executive committee minutes referencing cybersecurity risk ownership
Leadership communications (e.g., all-staff emails, town halls) promoting cybersecurity culture
Cybersecurity dashboard or KPI report presented to executive leadership
Budget allocations demonstrating leadership investment in cybersecurity

items.name: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, and enforced
items.desc: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, and enforced.
achieved: A RACI or responsibility assignment matrix defines cybersecurity roles across the organisation.
Role descriptions for key cybersecurity positions (CISO, risk owners, asset owners) are documented.
Cybersecurity responsibilities are incorporated into job descriptions and performance objectives.
Accountability for cybersecurity outcomes is enforced through performance management processes.
evidence: RACI chart or responsibility matrix for cybersecurity processes
Job descriptions for CISO, security team roles, and risk/asset owners
HR records showing cybersecurity responsibilities in performance objectives
Evidence of accountability being enforced (e.g., performance reviews, escalation records)

items.name: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
items.desc: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies.
achieved: The cybersecurity budget is formally approved and aligned with the organisation's risk profile and strategy.
Staffing levels for cybersecurity functions are reviewed against workload and risk requirements.
Technology, tools, and services required to fulfil cybersecurity responsibilities are funded.
Resource constraints are identified as risks and escalated to leadership for decision.
evidence: Cybersecurity budget documentation with leadership approval
Headcount plan for cybersecurity function compared to industry benchmarks
Asset register of security tools funded and operational
Risk records where resource constraints have been identified and escalated

items.name: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
items.desc: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices (e.g., de-provisioning, personnel actions).
achieved: Background screening procedures include cybersecurity considerations appropriate to role sensitivity.
Onboarding processes include cybersecurity awareness training and policy acknowledgement.
Offboarding procedures ensure timely revocation of all logical and physical access.
Role changes trigger access reviews to ensure privileges remain appropriate.
evidence: HR screening policy referencing information security vetting requirements
Onboarding checklist including security training completion and policy sign-off
Offboarding checklist with access revocation steps and completion records
Access review records triggered by role changes

sections.name: Policy
sections.desc: Organisational cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, and enforced

items.name: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
items.desc: A policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organisational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities.
achieved: A formal Information Security Policy (or equivalent) is documented, approved, and published.
The policy addresses the organisation's specific risk context, obligations, and strategic priorities.
The policy is communicated to all relevant personnel and third parties.
The policy is enforced through management controls and disciplinary procedures.
evidence: Board or executive-approved Information Security Policy
Policy acknowledgement records (e.g., staff sign-off logs, e-learning completions)
Evidence of policy being referenced in supplier contracts and onboarding processes
Disciplinary or enforcement records where policy violations have been addressed

items.name: Policy is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
items.desc: Policy is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organisational mission.
achieved: Policies are reviewed at defined intervals (at least annually) or when triggered by significant changes.
A policy review process ensures that changes in law, regulation, technology, or threat landscape are reflected.
Updated policies are re-communicated to affected stakeholders with version control maintained.
Policy version history is retained and accessible for audit purposes.
evidence: Policy review log with dates, reviewers, and change summaries
Version-controlled policy documents with change history
Communication records for policy updates (e.g., email notifications, re-acknowledgements)
Trigger events documentation showing policy review initiated by regulatory or threat changes

sections.name: Oversight
sections.desc: Results of organisation-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

items.name: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
items.desc: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction.
achieved: A management review process evaluates the effectiveness of the cybersecurity risk management strategy.
Key risk indicators (KRIs) and performance metrics are tracked and reviewed by leadership.
Outcomes of risk assessments and treatment activities feed back into strategic planning.
The cybersecurity strategy is updated based on review findings and changing business context.
evidence: Management review meeting minutes with cybersecurity risk outcomes discussed
KRI/KPI dashboard or report presented to leadership
Evidence of strategy updates following review outcomes
Cybersecurity programme review reports

items.name: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
items.desc: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organisational requirements and risks.
achieved: The risk management strategy is formally reviewed at least annually against organisational requirements.
Coverage gaps identified during reviews are addressed through strategy updates.
Emerging risk areas (e.g., new technologies, supply chain changes) are incorporated into the strategy.
Strategy changes are documented and approved by appropriate leadership.
evidence: Annual cybersecurity strategy review documentation
Gap analysis comparing current strategy against emerging risks
Approval records for strategy amendments
Board or executive committee papers on cybersecurity strategy

items.name: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
items.desc: Organisational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed.
achieved: Performance metrics for the cybersecurity programme are defined, measured, and reported.
Metrics cover both process effectiveness (e.g., patch compliance, training completion) and outcome measures (e.g., incident rates).
Underperformance against targets triggers formal investigation and corrective action.
Performance evaluation results are used to prioritise improvement investments.
evidence: Cybersecurity KPI/KRI framework with defined targets
Regular performance reports showing metric trends over time
Corrective action records linked to underperforming metrics
Evidence that performance results have influenced resource allocation or programme changes

sections.name: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
sections.desc: Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organisational stakeholders

items.name: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
items.desc: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management programme, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.
achieved: A formal C-SCRM policy and programme is documented and approved by leadership.
C-SCRM objectives are aligned with the organisation's overall cybersecurity and business strategy.
Roles and responsibilities for supply chain risk management are assigned and communicated.
C-SCRM processes cover the full supplier lifecycle from selection through offboarding.
evidence: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management policy and programme documentation
Leadership approval records for C-SCRM strategy
RACI for supply chain risk management roles
Supplier lifecycle management process documentation

items.name: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
items.desc: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally.
achieved: Supplier agreements clearly define cybersecurity responsibilities, obligations, and expectations.
Internal roles for managing supplier cybersecurity relationships are assigned.
Communication channels with key suppliers for cybersecurity matters are established.
Customer-facing cybersecurity obligations are documented and fulfilled.
evidence: Supplier contracts with cybersecurity clauses defining roles and responsibilities
Internal role descriptions for supplier relationship managers with cybersecurity scope
Communication records with key suppliers on cybersecurity topics
Customer security questionnaire responses or security assurance documentation

items.name: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
items.desc: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes.
achieved: Supply chain risks appear in the enterprise risk register.
Supplier risk assessments feed into the overall cybersecurity risk assessment process.
Supply chain risk findings trigger improvements to internal controls where appropriate.
C-SCRM metrics are included in enterprise risk reporting.
evidence: Enterprise risk register with supply chain risk entries
Supplier risk assessment reports integrated with enterprise risk process
Evidence of supply chain risk findings driving control improvements
C-SCRM metrics in enterprise risk dashboards or reports

items.name: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
items.desc: Suppliers are known and prioritised by criticality.
achieved: A comprehensive supplier register is maintained and kept current.
Suppliers are classified by criticality based on the data they handle, services they provide, and business impact of failure.
High-criticality suppliers receive enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring.
The supplier register is reviewed and updated at defined intervals.
evidence: Supplier register with criticality ratings and classification criteria
Evidence of criticality assessment methodology applied to all significant suppliers
Enhanced due diligence records for high-criticality suppliers
Records of periodic supplier register review and update

items.name: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
items.desc: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritised, and integrated into contracts and other agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties.
achieved: Minimum cybersecurity requirements for suppliers are defined based on risk and criticality tier.
Cybersecurity requirements are included in all significant supplier contracts and procurement documents.
Requirements are reviewed when renewing or amending supplier agreements.
Compliance with contractual cybersecurity requirements is assessed as part of supplier management.
evidence: Supplier cybersecurity requirements specification (tiered by criticality)
Contract templates or clauses referencing cybersecurity obligations
Evidence of requirements being incorporated into specific supplier contracts
Supplier audit or assessment reports evaluating compliance with contractual requirements

items.name: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
items.desc: Planning and due diligence are conducted to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships.
achieved: A pre-engagement due diligence process is applied to all significant third parties before contract award.
Due diligence covers cybersecurity posture, financial stability, certifications, and incident history.
Risk assessments are completed and documented before onboarding high-risk suppliers.
Due diligence findings are used to negotiate appropriate contractual protections.
evidence: Pre-engagement due diligence questionnaire or checklist
Due diligence assessment reports for significant suppliers
Pre-contract risk assessment documentation
Evidence that due diligence findings influenced contract terms or supplier selection decisions

items.name: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
items.desc: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are identified, recorded, prioritised, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship.
achieved: Supplier risks are recorded in the risk register and reviewed at defined intervals.
Risk monitoring activities (e.g., periodic assessments, audit rights, questionnaires) are conducted throughout the relationship.
Changes in supplier risk profile (e.g., security incidents, financial distress) trigger re-assessment.
Risk treatment actions for supplier risks are tracked to completion.
evidence: Supplier risk register with ongoing risk entries per supplier
Periodic supplier risk assessment records and schedules
Records of risk re-assessment triggered by supplier incidents or changes
Risk treatment action tracker for supply chain risks

items.name: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
items.desc: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities.
achieved: The incident response plan identifies key suppliers and their roles in incident scenarios.
Contact details and escalation procedures for critical suppliers are maintained and tested.
Suppliers are notified of relevant incidents per contractual and regulatory obligations.
Joint exercises or tabletop tests include critical suppliers where appropriate.
evidence: Incident response plan referencing key supplier contacts and responsibilities
Supplier contact and escalation directory maintained and tested
Incident notification records to suppliers and third parties
Records of joint incident response exercises with critical suppliers

items.name: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
items.desc: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programmes, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle.
achieved: C-SCRM practices are embedded across all lifecycle stages: procurement, onboarding, operations, and offboarding.
Key performance indicators for supply chain security are defined and tracked.
Security requirements for technology products address the full product lifecycle including end-of-life.
Supply chain security performance is reviewed as part of the enterprise cybersecurity programme review.
evidence: C-SCRM lifecycle process documentation covering all stages
Supply chain security KPIs with measurement records
Technology product lifecycle security requirements (including EOL provisions)
Enterprise risk programme review reports referencing supply chain security performance

items.name: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
items.desc: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement.
achieved: Offboarding procedures define how access, data, and assets are managed at contract conclusion.
Data return, destruction, or transfer requirements are specified in contracts and enforced on termination.
Transition plans are developed for critical suppliers to ensure service continuity.
Post-termination obligations (e.g., confidentiality, data retention) are documented and enforced.
evidence: Supplier offboarding checklist covering access revocation, data handling, and asset return
Contract clauses specifying post-termination data and confidentiality obligations
Transition or exit plan for critical suppliers
Evidence of post-termination obligations being fulfilled (e.g., data destruction certificates)

groups.name: IDENTIFY
groups.desc: The organisation's current cybersecurity risks are understood. This function supports identifying and prioritising the assets, vulnerabilities, threats, and risks most important to the organisation.

sections.name: Asset Management
sections.desc: Assets (data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organisation to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organisational objectives and the organisation's risk strategy

items.name: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
items.desc: Inventories of hardware managed by the organisation are maintained.
achieved: A comprehensive hardware asset inventory is maintained covering all managed endpoints, servers, network devices, and peripherals.
The inventory is kept current through automated discovery tools and manual processes.
Each hardware asset record includes owner, location, classification, and support status.
The inventory is reconciled against procurement and disposal records at defined intervals.
evidence: Hardware asset inventory (e.g., CMDB or asset management tool export)
Automated network discovery tool reports
Asset inventory reconciliation records
Procedures for asset registration on procurement and decommission

items.name: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
items.desc: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organisation are maintained.
achieved: A comprehensive software inventory covers all applications, operating systems, middleware, and cloud services.
Software is authorised before deployment and only authorised software is permitted to execute.
Licence management is integrated with the software inventory.
The inventory includes SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS services in addition to on-premises software.
evidence: Software asset inventory or CMDB software records
Software authorisation or whitelist policy
Licence management records
Cloud service inventory including SaaS and IaaS

items.name: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
items.desc: Representations of the organisation's authorised network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained.
achieved: Network diagrams depict the current architecture including all connected systems, network zones, and external connections.
Data flow diagrams document how sensitive data traverses the network, including cloud and third-party connections.
Authorised communication paths are defined and deviations are flagged for review.
Network and data flow documentation is reviewed and updated when significant changes are made.
evidence: Current network architecture diagrams
Data flow diagrams covering personal data and sensitive information flows
Authorised connection list or network access control documentation
Change records showing network documentation updated following changes

items.name: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
items.desc: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained.
achieved: A register of all third-party services used by the organisation is maintained.
Each supplier service record includes the data processed, criticality, and contractual status.
The supplier service inventory is linked to the asset inventory and risk register.
The inventory is reviewed and updated when new services are onboarded or terminated.
evidence: Third-party service register with service details and contract references
Evidence of linkage between supplier service inventory and risk register
Records of inventory updates following service onboarding or offboarding
Periodic review records for the supplier service inventory

items.name: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
items.desc: Assets are prioritised based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission.
achieved: An asset classification scheme defines tiers based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements.
Assets are labelled or tagged with their classification and criticality rating.
Critical and high-value assets receive enhanced protection proportionate to their classification.
Asset criticality ratings inform risk assessment prioritisation and control selection.
evidence: Asset classification policy and scheme documentation
Asset inventory with classification and criticality ratings applied
Controls matrix showing enhanced protections for critical assets
Risk assessments demonstrating asset criticality informing risk priority

items.name: Personnel are inventoried
items.desc: Inventories of the organisation's personnel are maintained.
achieved: A current inventory of personnel with access to organisational systems is maintained.
The personnel inventory is linked to identity and access management records.
Contractor and third-party personnel with system access are included in the inventory.
The personnel inventory is updated promptly when individuals join, move roles, or leave.
evidence: HR or identity management system records serving as personnel inventory
Contractor and third-party access register linked to personnel inventory
Joiner-mover-leaver process records showing inventory kept current
Periodic reconciliation of personnel inventory against access management records

items.name: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
items.desc: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained.
achieved: A data inventory identifies and classifies key data types (personal data, financial data, IP, etc.).
Data records include metadata: classification, owner, location, retention period, and legal basis for processing.
The data inventory supports compliance with data protection regulations.
Data inventory is reviewed and updated when new data types are collected or processed.
evidence: Data inventory or data register with metadata for key data types
Data classification policy with defined data types and handling requirements
Records of Information Activities (ROIA) or Article 30 records (GDPR)
Periodic review records for the data inventory

items.name: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
items.desc: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles.
achieved: Lifecycle management policies define requirements for each lifecycle stage: acquisition, operation, maintenance, and disposal.
End-of-life planning for hardware and software is proactive, avoiding unsupported assets in production.
Data lifecycle policies define retention, archival, and disposal requirements.
Lifecycle events (commissioning, decommissioning, disposal) are recorded in the asset inventory.
evidence: Asset lifecycle management policy
End-of-life register tracking assets approaching or past vendor support end dates
Data retention and disposal policy with evidence of implementation
Asset decommission and disposal records

sections.name: Risk Assessment
sections.desc: The cybersecurity risk to the organisation, assets, and individuals is understood by the organisation

items.name: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
items.desc: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.
achieved: Vulnerability scanning is performed on all in-scope assets at defined intervals (at least quarterly).
Scan findings are validated, de-duplicated, and recorded in a vulnerability register.
Vulnerabilities are prioritised using a risk-based approach (e.g., CVSS scores combined with asset criticality).
Vulnerability remediation timelines are defined by severity and tracked to completion.
evidence: Vulnerability scan reports from authenticated scans
Vulnerability register with severity ratings, owners, and remediation deadlines
Evidence of vulnerability prioritisation methodology applied
Remediation tracking records and closure evidence

items.name: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
items.desc: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources.

achieved: Forensic analysis procedures guide evidence collection and chain of custody.
Root cause analysis is conducted following significant incidents.
Analysis findings document the timeline, attack vector, and scope of compromise.
Root cause findings drive corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
evidence: Forensic analysis procedures and chain of custody documentation
Post-incident analysis reports with root cause findings
Incident timeline reconstructions with supporting log evidence
Corrective action records linked to root cause findings

items.name: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded to preserve the integrity of the investigation and evidentiary data
items.desc: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded to preserve the integrity of the investigation and evidentiary data.
achieved: An investigation log captures all analyst actions during the investigation.
Evidence is collected and preserved using forensically sound procedures.
Chain of custody is maintained for all evidence collected.
Investigation records are protected from tampering or deletion.
evidence: Investigation log records with timestamps and analyst actions
Evidence collection procedures and chain of custody forms
Forensic tool usage records and integrity verification
Evidence storage procedures protecting integrity of collected data

items.name: Incident data and metadata are collected and their integrity and provenance are preserved
items.desc: Incident data and metadata are collected and their integrity and provenance are preserved.
achieved: Incident data collection procedures define what data to collect and how to preserve integrity.
Metadata including timestamps and source information is preserved with collected data.
Data integrity is verified using hashing or digital signatures.
Data provenance is documented to support admissibility if legal proceedings arise.
evidence: Incident data collection procedures
Data integrity verification records (hash values for collected evidence)
Metadata preservation procedures and records
Chain of custody and provenance documentation for incident evidence

items.name: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
items.desc: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated.
achieved: Magnitude assessment procedures guide estimation of the number of affected systems and individuals.
Data loss or exposure estimates are calculated based on system access and data classification.
Magnitude assessments are validated as additional information becomes available.
Magnitude estimates inform regulatory notification obligations and public communication.
evidence: Magnitude assessment procedures in incident response documentation
Incident records showing magnitude estimates calculated and validated
Data exposure estimation methodology
Records of magnitude assessment influencing notification decisions

sections.name: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
sections.desc: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

items.name: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents in a timely manner
items.desc: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents in a timely manner.
achieved: Notification procedures define which stakeholders are to be notified for each incident category and severity.
Regulatory notification timelines are embedded in procedures (e.g., 72-hour GDPR, sector-specific requirements).
Internal notification reaches affected business units, leadership, and support teams promptly.
Notification records are maintained as part of the incident log.
evidence: Incident notification procedures with stakeholder-specific timelines
Regulatory notification records with timestamps
Internal incident notification records
Notification template library for different incident types

items.name: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders as defined by the incident response plan
items.desc: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders.
achieved: Information sharing procedures define what information can be shared externally and with whom.
Threat intelligence and incident information is shared with relevant ISACs, regulators, and partners.
Information classification guides determine what incident details can be disclosed.
External information sharing is conducted in a manner that does not compromise investigations.
evidence: Information sharing policy and procedures
Records of information shared with ISACs, regulators, and partners during incidents
Information classification criteria applied to incident data
Evidence of coordinated disclosure where external sharing occurred

sections.name: Incident Mitigation
sections.desc: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

items.name: Incidents are contained
items.desc: Incidents are contained.
achieved: Containment strategies are defined for common incident types (malware, account compromise, data exfiltration).
Short-term containment actions (isolation, blocking, disabling) are executed rapidly to limit impact.
Long-term containment maintains business operations while eradication is planned.
Containment actions and their effectiveness are documented in the incident record.
evidence: Incident containment playbooks per incident type
Incident records showing containment actions taken and timelines
Evidence of automated containment capabilities (e.g., EDR isolation features)
Containment effectiveness assessment in post-incident review

items.name: Incidents are eradicated
items.desc: Incidents are eradicated.
achieved: Eradication procedures remove the root cause and all artefacts of the incident.
Eradication activities include malware removal, patching, credential resets, and configuration corrections.
Eradication is verified before recovery activities begin.
Eradication findings feed into root cause analysis.
evidence: Incident eradication procedures
Eradication verification records (e.g., clean scan results, patching records)
Incident records showing eradication completed before recovery
Root cause analysis incorporating eradication findings

groups.name: RECOVER
groups.desc: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored. The RECOVER function supports timely restoration of normal operations and services impaired by a cybersecurity incident.

sections.name: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
sections.desc: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

items.name: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
items.desc: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process.
achieved: The recovery plan is activated following confirmation of incident containment and eradication.
Recovery team roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and exercised.
Recovery activities follow documented procedures to ensure consistent and effective restoration.
Recovery progress is tracked and communicated to management and affected stakeholders.
evidence: Recovery plan with defined roles, responsibilities, and procedures
Recovery exercise records demonstrating plan execution
Incident records showing recovery plan activated and followed
Recovery progress communication records

items.name: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
items.desc: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritised, and performed.
achieved: Recovery actions are prioritised based on business criticality and RTO requirements.
Scope of recovery is determined from the impact assessment conducted during the incident.
Recovery actions are sequenced to restore the most critical services first.
Recovery activities are performed by trained personnel following tested procedures.
evidence: Recovery prioritisation criteria based on business criticality and RTO
Impact assessment records informing recovery scope
Recovery action sequencing documentation
Evidence of recovery personnel training and competency

items.name: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them in restoration
items.desc: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration.
achieved: Backup integrity checks are performed before restoration to confirm backups are clean and complete.
Restoration test procedures verify that backups can be successfully restored.
Backups used in recovery are verified against known-good baselines where available.
Verification failures trigger escalation and use of alternative recovery assets.
evidence: Backup integrity verification procedures
Backup restore test records demonstrating successful verification
Recovery records showing integrity checks performed before restoration
Escalation records for backup verification failures

items.name: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
items.desc: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms.
achieved: Post-incident operational baseline is defined based on critical mission function requirements.
Residual risk from the incident is assessed and accepted or treated before returning to normal operations.
Enhanced monitoring is applied following restoration to detect recurrence.
Return to normal operational norms is formally declared by authorised management.
evidence: Post-incident operational baseline documentation
Residual risk assessment records following incident recovery
Enhanced monitoring records applied post-incident
Formal declaration of return to normal operations with management sign-off

items.name: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
items.desc: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed.
achieved: Restored systems are validated against security baselines before being returned to production.
Integrity verification includes checking for persistent threats, configuration correctness, and data completeness.
Service restoration is confirmed with affected business units before closing the incident.
Normal operating status declaration is documented in the incident record.
evidence: System validation procedures applied post-restoration
Security baseline compliance checks for restored systems
Service restoration confirmation records from business units
Incident closure records with normal operating status confirmed

items.name: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
items.desc: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed.
achieved: Criteria for incident closure are defined and consistently applied.
All incident-related documentation is completed and filed before closure.
Lessons learned are captured and fed into the improvement process.
Incident closure is formally authorised by the incident commander or designated authority.
evidence: Incident closure criteria and declaration procedures
Complete incident records including all analysis and action documentation
Lessons learned reports generated from closed incidents
Formal incident closure authorisation records

sections.name: Incident Recovery Communication
sections.desc: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

items.name: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
items.desc: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders.
achieved: A communication plan defines what recovery information is shared with internal and external stakeholders.
Regular status updates are provided to management, customers, and partners during recovery.
Recovery communication is accurate, timely, and appropriate for the audience.
Communication records are maintained as part of the incident documentation.
evidence: Recovery communication plan or procedures
Status update records sent to internal and external stakeholders during recovery
Customer or partner notification records during significant recovery events
Communication log as part of incident documentation

items.name: Public updates on incidents and recovery activities are shared using approved messaging and channels
items.desc: Public updates on incidents and recovery activities are shared using approved messaging and channels.
achieved: A public communications process defines approval requirements for external statements during incidents.
Communications and PR teams are engaged for significant incidents with public impact.
Approved messaging templates are prepared in advance for common incident scenarios.
All public communications are reviewed for accuracy and legal compliance before release.
evidence: Public communications approval process for incident-related statements
Crisis communications plan referencing PR and communications team involvement
Pre-approved messaging templates for common incident scenarios
Records of public communications reviewed and approved before release
